 Mississippi U.S. Senate race undecided a week after Election Day 
 Colom leads Hyde-Smith by more than 2,800 votes in unofficial results as counties review ballots. 
 The race for U.S. Senate in Mississippi remains undecided a week after the election. By Courtney Ann Jackson Published : Nov. 10, 2026 at 10:37 PM CST | Updated : 30 minutes ago Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google JACKSON, Miss. (WLBT) - One week after Election Day, Mississippi’s U.S. Senate race remains undecided, with Democrat Scott Colom leading Republican Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith by more than 2,800 votes in unofficial results.
 Counties are reviewing outstanding ballots, and the close contest is bringing new attention to how votes are counted.
 Hinds County works through affidavit ballots
 Hinds County, the state’s most populous county, is working through its affidavit ballots as observers watch.
 Former Mississippi Republican Party Chairman Lucien Smith said what is happening after Election Day is not new, but more people are paying attention this year.
 “The big thing that I think people are likely missing, the vote count always changes between what you see on Tuesday night and what is in the final vote total. The difference is most of us stop paying attention on election night,” Smith said.
 Presley calls for uniform process, early voting
 Brandon Presley, the 2023 Democratic nominee for governor, said the scrutiny is exposing problems he believes have existed all along. He said Mississippi needs a more uniform election process and wants lawmakers to allow early voting.
 “We’ve got an unmitigated mess in how Mississippi’s election system goes. This is the first time that we just had this amount of national scrutiny,” Presley said.
 Differing views on who will win
 Colom leads Hyde-Smith in unofficial results, but ballots are still being reviewed and the race remains undecided.
 Smith said it is too early to know who won. He said he hopes the remaining affidavit ballots favor Hyde-Smith.
 “I don’t think there’s any way to know today who is going to be the winner. I certainly hope it’s Cindy Hyde-Smith. I’m optimistic that the affidavit ballots are going to break clearly in her direction, but it’s statistically a tie,” Smith said.
 Presley said he believes Colom’s lead will hold and that Hyde-Smith should concede. He expects the remaining Hinds County ballots to favor Colom.
 “If there’s a path to victory, then you need to believe in Santa Claus, the tooth fairy and some ocean front property in Arizona. There’s no path to victory,” Presley said.
 Certification deadline
 Counties have until Friday to certify their results as eligible ballots continue to be processed.
